company_news.headline: AMZN Q2 Deep Dive: AI-Driven AWS Growth and Cost Leverage Shape Outlook
company_news.summary: Cloud computing and online retail behemoth Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) beat Wall Street’s revenue expectations in Q2 CY2026, with sales up 19.6% year on year to $200.6 billion. On the other hand, next quarter’s revenue guidance of $199.5 billion was less impressive, coming in 2.1% below analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $5.75 per share was significantly above analysts’ consensus estimates.

company_news.headline: Wall Street ends higher as Amazon soothes AI jitters
company_news.summary: STORY: Wall Street ended higher on Friday, with the Dow adding more than half a percent, the S&P 500 gaining seven-tenths of a percent and the Nasdaq climbing one percent.:: AmazonAmazon surged more than 15% after the tech giant posted its biggest quarterly revenue growth in over four years. Its results, along with a similar report from Microsoft this week, alleviated investor concerns about potential overspending on AI data centers.Meanwhile, shares of Apple tumbled more than 7% after a disappointing forecast showed that the iPhone maker was struggling to secure enough components, as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains.Friday marked the end of a bumpy week for stocks that included a Fed policy meeting in which the central bank left rates unchanged - but with three dissenters pushing for a 25 basis point hike.Dean Smith is chief strategist & portfolio manager at FolioBeyond."I think there was a decent case to be made that a hike is in order. Inflation, we had a slightly softer print on the most recent one, but inflation is now running well above Fed's 2% stated target. It's higher now than it was a year ago and it seems to be reaccelerating. [FLASH] So it was a close call probably, but I think, you know, if I had been on that voting committee, I would have voted for a rate hike as well.":: ArchiveOther stocks on the move Friday included Monolithic Power Systems, which rose more than 8% after forecasting third-quarter revenue above estimates.But shares of GoDaddy slid nearly 17% after the domain registrar narrowed its annual revenue forecast.

company_news.headline: Market Talk: Apple sinks, Amazon soars in split verdict on AI winners
company_news.summary: STORY: :: Recorded on July 31:: Lisa Bernhard, Reuters:: Dean Smith, Portfolio Manager, FolioBeyondShares of Apple tumbled as much as 10% on Friday after a disappointing forecast showed that the iPhone maker was struggling to secure enough components as the AI-driven data center boom strains global supply chains.The drop, if sustained, would erase nearly $500 billion from Apple's market capitalization and return the crown of the world's most valuable company to AI chip giant Nvidia, days after reclaiming it.Meanwhile, shares of Amazon soared as much as 15% after the tech giant's solid cloud sales growth reinforced investor confidence in its massive AI bets."There's two really different trends going on," said Smith. "One is the hardware constraint, the [other is] cloud compute capacity, and those are going to continue to drive what we see in the AI investment thesis."Next week, the focus will remain on AI when SpaceX delivers its first quarterly earnings results since going public."There's no mystery about how many rockets they're firing off, we can see them," said Dean with a laugh. "So what I'm looking for in SpaceX is to see what is their plan for the AI side of the business."
